summary: Approved. The saturated depth visualization fix is ready for user live-render validation; no Builder repair is required. Root cause analysis is plausible: finite min/max can be dominated by far-plane or outlier depths, compressing useful near-scene values into a very small viridis range. The implementation now computes per-setting 1st/99th percentile visualization bounds by default, supports explicit min/max meter overrides, and preserves raw metric .npy depth frames unchanged.

findings.message: examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:1310 saves depth directly with np.save(depth_frame_file, depth) before visualization, and examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:1332 generates viridis frames from saved .npy files, so clipping affects PNG/MP4 visualization only.

examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:1315 passes args.depth_visualization_min_meters and args.depth_visualization_max_meters into get_depth_visualization_bounds, and the helper only computes percentiles for bounds that are not explicit, so explicit overrides behave correctly.

The advanced --depth-visualization-max-samples option is validated and used in code but is not mentioned in examples/flashlight/README.md or docs/running_our_example_applications.md. This is a documentation completeness gap, not a blocker for live-render validation.
